sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Ideological Shift**: Transition from 'Political Mendicancy' to 'Atma-Shakti' (Self-reliance) and **Swaraj** as the primary goal.
• **Methodology**: Adoption of **Passive Resistance**, **Boycott** of foreign goods, and promotion of **Swadeshi** (indigenous) institutions.
• **Mass Base**: Shift from elite-led intellectual debates to involving students, women, and the urban working class.
• **Key Metric**: The **Surat Split (1907)** serves as the definitive institutional rupture between the Moderates and the Extremists.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Lala Lajpat Rai (Punjab), Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Maharashtra), Bipin Chandra Pal (Bengal)

items.definition: A strategy of non-cooperation with the colonial administration, including refusal to pay taxes or serve in government offices.
Establishment of the National Council of Education (1906) to replace colonial-controlled universities with indigenous curricula.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Swadeshi Stores**: Promotion of indigenous textiles and goods to cripple British economic interests.
• **Vernacular Press**: Use of 'Kesari' and 'Maratha' to disseminate radical nationalist ideas.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Lack of a unified national organization after the Surat Split; severe government repression (Sedition Acts).
• **Solutions**: Eventual reunification at Lucknow Session (1916) and the rise of the Home Rule League.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'LAL-BAL-PAL-AU'
• **Decoded Meaning**: **L**ala Lajpat Rai, **B**al Gangadhar Tilak, **P**al (Bipin Chandra), **A**urobindo Ghosh, **U**nited (Surat Split context).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Extremists did not advocate for 'armed revolution' as a primary policy in the 1905-1907 phase; they advocated for 'passive resistance' and 'mass agitation'.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Political Mendicancy' when describing the Moderate phase to contrast with the 'Assertive Nationalism' of the Extremists.

keyTakeaways: Extremists transformed the national movement from a petition-based approach to a mass-mobilization strategy.
The Surat Split (1907) was the culmination of ideological differences regarding the scope and methods of the Swadeshi movement.
The movement laid the groundwork for the Gandhian era by proving the efficacy of mass participation and boycott.
